originalTitle: The most beautiful London game ever🥹 #chess #worldchesschampionship #dingliren #chessnest
transcript: If you need to cut a tree in an hour, you're going to spend the first 45 minutes sharpening the axe. And that is exactly what the exchess champion Dingly Ren did with this masterpiece of a game. After opening the game with a very controversial London system for the first time in the history of the World Chess Championship, he managed to get to better position in an endame. But the win was far from clear. I didn't see a knockout blow here. And the chess world was stunned and confused when Dingly Ren uncorked the move D5. What is this pawn doing? had changed. And even the computer thought that this was a mistake because not even the computer could predict what was about to happen. No one could see the point of this move apart from Dingly Ren himself. He sees it. He sees it. You know, this is the remarkable part. He sees it. And just a couple of moves after that, Ian Neponi thought that he was in the clear after shuffling his king and protecting the mating square. He was about to get a new queen on the edge of the board. But then he was hit with the cold shower. Queen F7. And in this position, he resigned. Actually, you are all about here. The computer starts begging black to sacrifice all of its pieces just to try and delay the inevitable, but it's not going to work. The point is that the queen is going to sacrifice itself for a checkmate with the knight and the rook. And there's nothing that black can do about it. And if the black king tries to go out into the center of the board, well, now we see the final point of this pawn push that was played six moves prior. And just like that, Dinglan had ensured the London system to have a 100% win rate in the World Chess Championships.
